title: Consolidate control-plane partitioning strategy and reduce tenant query costs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Over time the control-plane Postgres schema accumulated inconsistent partitioning strategies across several high-churn tables (events, audit_logs, tenant_metrics). This causes uneven hotspotting, unpredictable planner choices, and high tail query costs for tenant-scoped reads. Symptoms observed in production: slow tenant listing queries, frequent sequential scans on audit_logs during retention compaction, and incident #INC-2025-02-03 where a bulk backfill caused cascading read latency.
updates: 2025-02-10 - Ticket created by Maya: outlined symptoms, linked recent incidents and slow query samples. Proposed consolidation to a unified partitioning pattern and incremental online migration approach.

2025-02-12 - Design sync w/ infra and schema owners. Agreed candidate strategy: time-range partitioning for high-write append tables + tenant-hash sub-partitions for very large tenants; introduce a lightweight tenant hot-table index for top 1% tenants.

2025-02-15 - Benchmarks: PoC on staging (audit_logs) shows 3x reduction in median tenant-scan time when querying partition-pruned snapshot vs current. Remaining issues: planner still chooses seq scan for small, highly selective predicates unless partial indexes exist.

2025-02-18 - Decision: adopt a two-pronged approach: 1) canonicalize partitioning scheme (range by ingest_date, hash on tenant_id for >10M rows), 2) create targeted partial indexes and predicate-stable statistics for tenant-heavy queries. Added metrics and tracing events to measure partition pruning quality.

2025-02-20 - Migration plan drafted: stepwise online migration for each table (audit_logs -> events -> tenant_metrics). Each step includes chunked COPY TO/COPY FROM with tenant throttling, a background worker to move cold partitions first, and a fast rollback path by toggling a view to the legacy table until new partitions are verified.
2025-02-24 - Final sign-off requested from DBAs and SRE. Assignee updated to Arjun. Added due date and estimate. Opening initial PR for audit_logs partition schema (link in attachments).
acceptance_criteria: All targeted tables (audit_logs, events, tenant_metrics) have canonical partitioning applied in staging and are validated against query patterns from the slow query log.
Online migration tooling moves partitions in bounded-rate batches without violating SLOs; we have documented throttles and can pause/resume migration jobs.
End-to-end tests (integration + load) show at least 40% reduction in 95th percentile tenant-scoped read latency for affected routes.
Partial indexes and updated statistics prevent regression where planner picks sequential scans for small selective tenant queries.
Monitoring dashboards (partition pruning ratio, migration lag, per-tenant read cost) are created and have alerting thresholds configured.
Rollback mechanism validated: toggling the control-plane view reverts reads to legacy table with <30s failover during migration.
Runbook updated and a post-mortem template prepared for any migration-related incidents.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Long-running migration jobs could overload replicas and cause read SLO breaches. Mitigation: implement a rate-limiter in the mover job, and autosuspend during emergency incident windows.
Risk: Incorrect planner behavior after schema change causing regressions. Mitigation: ship in staging with realistic replayed traffic and add an AB test gating in production.
Risk: Disk blow-up from concurrent copy operations. Mitigation: limit parallelism and prefer ALTER TABLE ATTACH PARTITION patterns where possible.
Risk: Edge-case queries relying on legacy implicit ordering. Mitigation: run query compatibility suite and add deprecation warnings for affected APIs.
Risk: Migration tooling bug. Mitigation: small canary migrations on a subset of tenants (low-volume) and manual verification before scaling.
implementation_steps: 1) Finalize canonical partitioning DDLs and review with DBA (audit_logs staging PR ready).
2) Add planner-stability metrics and dashboard for partition pruning and index usage.
3) Build background mover worker: chunked export/import with tenant-aware backpressure and pause/resume endpoints.
4) Create partial indexes for top query patterns and update ANALYZE policies after partition changes.
5) Run full staging migration with realistic traffic replay; measure latency, cost, and disk usage.
6) Production rollout: canary on 10 low-volume tenants -> expand to 10% traffic -> full rollout with a maintenance window for last large tenants.
7) Post-rollout verification and decommission legacy partitioning artifacts.
8) Document runbooks and hand-off to platform on-call and runbook owners.
followups: ENG-82109 - Add automated tenant-size histogram generator and periodic compaction suggestions.
ENG-83210 - Investigate cost-aware query planner hints for federated reads across regions.
PM-412 - Communicate migration windows and expected impact to customer success for enterprise customers.
